places.name: Great Ocean Road
places.ai_summary: The Great Ocean Road is one of the world's most scenic coastal drives, stretching along Victoria's southwest coast. It features dramatic cliffs, pristine beaches, lush rainforests, and iconic landmarks like the Twelve Apostles. Visitors can enjoy breathtaking views, wildlife, and charming seaside towns.
places.cost: Free (scenic drive, some attractions may charge)
places.place_tip: Start early to enjoy the sunrise and stop at lookouts for the best photos.

attribution.title: 2009-0825-GreatOceanRoadsign
attribution.author: Bobak Ha'Eri
attribution.description: Sign at the eastern end of the Great Ocean Road, Australia.

places.name: Twelve Apostles
places.ai_summary: The Twelve Apostles are iconic limestone stacks rising majestically from the Southern Ocean along the Great Ocean Road. This natural wonder offers breathtaking views, dramatic sunsets, and a chance to witness the power of coastal erosion. Boardwalks and lookouts provide excellent photo opportunities.
places.place_tip: Visit at sunset for stunning colors and fewer crowds at the lookouts.
places.address: Great Ocean Road, Port Campbell VIC 3269, Australia

places.name: Phillip Island Penguin Parade
places.ai_summary: Phillip Island Penguin Parade is a world-famous wildlife experience where visitors can watch hundreds of little penguins waddle ashore at sunset. The site offers boardwalks, viewing platforms, and educational exhibits about penguin conservation.
places.place_tip: Dress warmly and book tickets in advance for the best viewing spots.

places.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)
places.ai_summary: The Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) is Australia's largest stadium and a historic venue for cricket, Australian football, and major events. Visitors can tour the stadium, visit the National Sports Museum, and experience the excitement of live matches.
places.place_tip: Book a guided tour for behind-the-scenes access and visit during a match for atmosphere.

places.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne
places.ai_summary: A lush oasis in the heart of Melbourne, the Royal Botanic Gardens feature over 8,500 plant species, tranquil lakes, and themed gardens. It's a perfect spot for relaxation, picnics, and nature walks.
places.place_tip: Bring a picnic and enjoy the lakeside lawns or join a guided walk.
places.address: Birdwood Ave, South Yarra VIC 3141, Australia

places.name: Federation Square
places.ai_summary: Federation Square is Melbourne’s cultural heart, hosting museums, galleries, restaurants, and public events. Its unique architecture and lively atmosphere make it a must-visit for locals and tourists alike.
places.place_tip: Check the event calendar for free public performances and exhibitions.
places.address: Swanston St & Flinders St, Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia

places.name: National Gallery of Victoria
places.ai_summary: Australia’s oldest and most visited art museum, the National Gallery of Victoria houses an extensive collection of international and Australian art. The gallery offers exhibitions, events, and educational programs for all ages.
places.place_tip: Visit on weekends for special exhibitions and family activities.
places.address: 180 St Kilda Rd, Melbourne VIC 3006, Australia

places.name: Yarra Valley Wineries
places.ai_summary: The Yarra Valley is Victoria’s premier wine region, known for its cool-climate wines, gourmet food, and scenic landscapes. Visitors can tour vineyards, taste award-winning wines, and enjoy local produce.
places.place_tip: Book a wine tour for easy transport and expert guidance.

places.name: Grampians National Park
places.ai_summary: Grampians National Park is renowned for its rugged mountain ranges, wildflowers, Aboriginal rock art, and panoramic lookouts. It’s a haven for hikers, climbers, and nature lovers.
places.place_tip: Visit in spring for wildflowers and clear hiking conditions.

places.name: Bright
places.ai_summary: Bright is a picturesque town in Victoria’s High Country, famous for its autumn colors, cycling trails, and proximity to alpine resorts. It’s a gateway to outdoor adventures and seasonal festivals.
places.place_tip: Visit in autumn for vibrant foliage and local food festivals.
places.advanced_booking: Recommended for accommodation in peak season

places.name: Sovereign Hill
places.ai_summary: Sovereign Hill is an open-air museum in Ballarat, recreating the gold rush era of the 1850s. Visitors can pan for gold, explore historic buildings, and enjoy live demonstrations and costumed characters.
places.place_tip: Arrive early to catch the gold pour demonstration and street performances.

places.name: Healesville Sanctuary
places.ai_summary: Healesville Sanctuary is a renowned wildlife park dedicated to native Australian animals. Visitors can see koalas, kangaroos, platypuses, and enjoy interactive keeper talks and animal encounters.
places.place_tip: Attend the Spirits of the Sky bird show for a memorable experience.
places.address: Glen Eadie Ave, Healesville VIC 3777, Australia

places.name: Puffing Billy Railway
places.ai_summary: Puffing Billy Railway is a century-old steam train that runs through the scenic Dandenong Ranges. It’s a nostalgic journey for families and train enthusiasts, with open-sided carriages and forest views.
places.place_tip: Book tickets in advance and sit on the open carriage for best views.
places.address: 1 Old Monbulk Rd, Belgrave VIC 3160, Australia

places.name: St Kilda Beach
places.ai_summary: St Kilda Beach is Melbourne’s most famous urban beach, known for its lively promenade, water sports, and sunset views. The area features cafes, Luna Park, and a colony of wild penguins.
places.place_tip: Visit at sunset for beautiful views and spot penguins on the pier.
places.address: St Kilda Beach, St Kilda VIC 3182, Australia

places.name: Ballarat Wildlife Park
places.ai_summary: Ballarat Wildlife Park is home to a wide variety of native Australian animals, including kangaroos, koalas, wombats, and crocodiles. The park offers interactive experiences and educational talks.
places.place_tip: Feed kangaroos and join keeper talks for close animal encounters.
places.address: 250 Fussell St, Ballarat East VIC 3350, Australia

places.name: Dandenong Ranges National Park
places.ai_summary: Dandenong Ranges National Park is a lush forested area near Melbourne, famous for its towering mountain ash trees, walking trails, and charming villages. It’s ideal for hiking, picnics, and birdwatching.
places.place_tip: Try the 1000 Steps Kokoda Track Memorial Walk for a scenic challenge.
places.address: Dandenong Ranges National Park, Victoria, Australia

places.name: Mornington Peninsula Hot Springs
places.ai_summary: Mornington Peninsula Hot Springs is a natural geothermal bathing and spa complex. Visitors can relax in thermal pools, enjoy spa treatments, and take in the tranquil gardens.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary for special events.

places.place_tip: Book spa treatments in advance for a complete wellness experience.

places.name: Wilsons Promontory National Park
places.ai_summary: Wilsons Promontory National Park is a coastal wilderness area with pristine beaches, granite mountains, and abundant wildlife. It’s ideal for hiking, camping, and nature photography.
places.place_tip: Book campsites early and hike to secluded beaches for stunning views.
places.address: Wilsons Promontory National Park, Victoria, Australia
